meaning.description: Herisau’s flag shows its arms: a black bear striding upright on white, a golden log on its shoulder. Like many places in the region, it goes back to the legend of St Gall, first written down in 771: the saint told a bear to fetch wood for his fire, and it came back with a heavy log. The black bear became the emblem of the Abbey of St. Gall in the 14th century; the shouldered log first appears on Herisau’s seal of 1401, and Herisau kept it.
